videos.title: Power BI Get Data: Choosing Import, DirectQuery, or Live Connections Explained
videos.description:
After watching this video, you'll confidently understand the differences between Import, DirectQuery, and Live connections in Power BI, enabling you to choose the best data connectivity mode for your reports.

Adam Saxton breaks down the three main ways to get data into Power BI Desktop: Import, DirectQuery, and Live connections. He explains how Import mode caches data inside Power BI for fast performance and full feature support, while DirectQuery queries data live from the source, useful for very large datasets but with some limitations. Live connections connect directly to Analysis Services or Power BI datasets without importing data, and Adam also covers composite models that combine these modes. Throughout, he provides practical examples and tips to help you optimize your Power BI data models and improve report performance.

✅ KEY TAKEAWAYS
Understand the benefits and limitations of Import mode in Power BI.
Learn when and how to use DirectQuery for large datasets and its performance considerations.
Discover what Live connections are and how they differ from DirectQuery.
Explore composite models to combine Import, DirectQuery, and Live connections in one report.
Gain practical tips on data modeling best practices like star schemas for better performance.

videos.title: How to Handle MULTIPLE Fact Tables in Power BI
videos.description:
Yooo! 🙌 take your data skills to the next level and join fellow data professionals in our community THE CUBE: https://guyinacube.com

When working with multiple fact tables, many Power BI authors end up duplicating dimensions or consolidating fact tables into a single table. Patrick explains why both approaches can create problems including larger models, slower refreshes, blank values, and more complicated measures. You'll see a practical walkthrough of using conformed dimensions like Date and Product across multiple fact tables, enabling accurate reporting and easier analysis in a single visual. This approach aligns with data warehouse modeling best practices and helps you build cleaner, more efficient Power BI semantic models.

✅ KEY TAKEAWAYS
Avoid duplicating dimension tables across multiple fact tables.
Consolidated fact tables can introduce blanks, larger models, and more complex DAX.
Use shared (conformed) dimensions such as Date and Product across fact tables.
Keep fact-specific dimensions connected only where they belong.
Shared dimensions allow measures from multiple facts to be compared in the same visual.
Add descriptions and guidance to measures and tables to help report authors avoid modeling mistakes.
